en.greeting: Hi! In B2 you met It is said that… and He is said to…. Today you'll report news like a journalist: more reporting verbs, three infinitive forms for three different times, and There is believed to be…. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Who says so?
steps.text: Quick recap from B2: It is said that this house is haunted. Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali. Now let's see why news writers love these patterns.
steps.body:
These patterns report what people say or believe **without naming who** and **without saying it's true**: the writer keeps a **distance from the claim**, so the tone stays formal and objective. You do the same in Indonesian with *Dikabarkan bahwa…*, *Diduga…*, *Konon…*.
Each reporting verb has a job: *expected* for the future, *estimated* for numbers, *known* for accepted facts, *alleged* for accusations that aren't proven yet (crime and court news).

steps.title: Pattern 1: It is thought that…
steps.text: Pattern 1 puts It at the start and the whole piece of news after that. be shows when the claim was made.
steps.body: **It + be + reporting verb (third form) + that + a full sentence.** The *that* part keeps its own subject, verb and tense. Three verbs work **only** here: *It is hoped / It was agreed / It has been decided that…* ('The rules are hoped to…' ✗).

examples.en: It is estimated that 10 million people use the app every day.
examples.id: Diperkirakan 10 juta orang memakai aplikasi itu setiap hari.

examples.en: It was reported that the flight had been delayed for six hours.
examples.id: Dikabarkan penerbangan itu tertunda enam jam.

examples.en: It is thought that the fire started in the warehouse.
examples.id: Kebakaran itu diduga bermula di gudang.

examples.en: It has been decided that the office will close on Fridays.
examples.id: Sudah diputuskan bahwa kantor akan tutup setiap hari Jumat.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A colleague forwards you some news about Dr. Wulan, a researcher at a university in Yogyakarta.

options: Dr. Wulan is said that she is moving to Geneva.
It is said Dr. Wulan to be moving to Geneva.
It is said that Dr. Wulan is moving to Geneva.
question.explanation: Pattern 1: **It is said that + a full sentence** (*Dr. Wulan is moving…*). The first option mixes the patterns: with *that*, start with **It**, not the person. The second puts a to-infinitive after *It is said*, but pattern 1 needs *that* + a full sentence.

steps.title: Pattern 2: three infinitives
steps.text: Pattern 2 starts with the person or thing in the news. The infinitive after it shows when the action happens.
steps.body:
**Subject + be + reporting verb + to-infinitive:**
- **to + base form** = now or in general (with *expected*: later)
- **to be + -ing** = in progress now (*sedang*)
- **to have + third form** = earlier (*sudah, kemarin*)
**The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian keeps one verb and adds a time word (*dikabarkan mengundurkan diri kemarin*). English shows the time in the infinitive: 'is reported **resign** yesterday' ✗, 'is reported to resign yesterday' ✗ → *is reported **to have resigned** yesterday*.

steps.title: When does the action happen?
steps.text: Here are the infinitives on a line. Each one shows the action's time compared with the moment people say or believe it.

timeline.title: The infinitive shows the time
timeline.caption: Measure from the moment of saying: is reported (now) or was reported (then).

marks.label: to be preparing · in progress now

steps.title: Same news, two patterns
steps.text: Watch how the verb after that becomes an infinitive when the person or thing moves to the front.
steps.body: Present → **to + base**; continuous → **to be + -ing**; past simple or present perfect → **to have + third form**. With a state verb (*be, own, know, cost*), use to + base: *She is thought to own three hotels*, not 'to be owning'.

examples.en: It is said that he lives in Bali. → He is said to live in Bali.
examples.id: Konon dia tinggal di Bali.

examples.en: It is believed that the bank is preparing a new app. → The bank is believed to be preparing a new app.
examples.id: Bank itu diyakini sedang menyiapkan aplikasi baru.

examples.en: It is reported that the singer has cancelled her tour. → The singer is reported to have cancelled her tour.
examples.id: Penyanyi itu dikabarkan sudah membatalkan turnya.

examples.en: It was thought that she was hiding in Medan. → She was thought to be hiding in Medan.
examples.id: Waktu itu dia diduga sedang bersembunyi di Medan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: An article about a listed company in Jakarta. Rewrite the news in pattern 2.

question.prompt: It is said that the director sold his shares before the announcement. → The director ___ his shares before the announcement.
question.explanation: The selling happened **earlier** (past simple *sold*, before the announcement) → **to have + third form**: *is said to have sold*. 'to sell' is for now or in general, and 'to sold' breaks the rule: after *to*, the base form (*have*).

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: A business news headline. Say it in English, in pattern 2.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Perusahaan itu diyakini sedang merencanakan PHK.
question.solution: The company is believed to be planning layoffs.
question.explanation: The company comes first, then **is believed** (diyakini). *sedang merencanakan* is in progress now → **to be + -ing**: *to be planning*. PHK = **layoffs**.

steps.title: Pattern 3: There is believed to be…
steps.text: When the news is that something exists (ada), the subject is there.
steps.body:
**There + is/are + reporting verb + to be + noun.** The verb agrees with the noun after it: *There **is** thought to be **a leak*** / *There **are** thought to be **two leaks***. For something earlier: **to have been** (*There is said to have been an argument*).
**The Indonesian trap:** in *Diduga **ada** masalah*, *ada* means *there is*, not *have*. 'There is believed **to have** a problem' ✗ → *There is believed **to be** a problem.*

pairs.en: There is said to have been…

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A guide at a national park in Kalimantan tells visitors about the plants.

question.prompt: Complete: ___ more than 300 species of orchid in the park.
question.explanation: *ada* = there are, so the infinitive is **to be**, and *300 species* is plural → **are**: *There are known to be*. 'There is' doesn't agree with the plural noun, and 'to have' is the *ada* trap.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here are the three patterns on one page. Keep it for your next report or news article.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · impersonal and advanced passive
artifact.intro: Report a claim without naming who made it or saying it's true. be shows when the claim was made; the infinitive shows when the action happened.
rows: It + be + third form + that + full sentence
It is estimated that 10 million people use the app.
It was reported that the flight had been delayed.
It has been decided that the office will close on Fridays.
He is thought to live in Bali.
The bank is believed to be preparing a new app.
The singer is reported to have cancelled her tour.
The bridge is expected to open in May.
There + is/are + third form + to be
There is thought to be a leak in the pipe.
There is said to have been an argument.
tips: Don't mix the patterns: **It … that** or **subject … to**. 'He is said that he left' ✗ → *It is said that he left* / *He is said to have left*.
After **to**, the base form, and the time goes into the infinitive: 'is reported resign yesterday' ✗ → **is reported to have resigned** yesterday.
After **there**, always **to be** (or to have been), never 'to have' + noun: *Diduga ada masalah* = *There is believed to be a problem*.

examples.en: Rice prices are expected to fall after the harvest.
examples.id: Harga beras diperkirakan turun setelah panen.

examples.en: The former manager is alleged to have stolen Rp2 billion.
examples.id: Mantan manajer itu diduga mencuri Rp2 miliar.

examples.en: The two banks are understood to be in talks.
examples.id: Kabarnya kedua bank itu sedang berunding.

examples.en: There are believed to be more than 700 languages in Indonesia.
examples.id: Diyakini ada lebih dari 700 bahasa di Indonesia.

id.greeting: Hai! Di B2 kamu sudah kenal It is said that… dan He is said to…. Hari ini kamu akan melaporkan berita seperti wartawan: lebih banyak kata kerja pelaporan, tiga bentuk infinitif untuk tiga waktu yang berbeda, dan There is believed to be…. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Siapa yang bilang?
steps.text: Ringkasan dari B2: It is said that this house is haunted. Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali. Sekarang kita lihat kenapa penulis berita suka sekali pola ini.
steps.body:
Pola ini melaporkan apa yang dikatakan atau diyakini orang **tanpa menyebut siapa** dan **tanpa menyatakan bahwa itu benar**: penulisnya menjaga **jarak dari klaim**, jadi nadanya tetap formal dan objektif. Kamu juga melakukannya dalam bahasa Indonesia dengan *Dikabarkan bahwa…*, *Diduga…*, *Konon…*.
Setiap kata kerja pelaporan punya tugas: *expected* untuk masa depan, *estimated* untuk angka, *known* untuk fakta yang sudah diakui, *alleged* untuk tuduhan yang belum terbukti (berita kriminal dan pengadilan).

steps.title: Pola 1: It is thought that…
steps.text: Pola 1 menaruh It di awal dan seluruh beritanya setelah that. be menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat.
steps.body: **It + be + kata kerja pelaporan (bentuk ketiga) + that + kalimat lengkap.** Bagian *that* tetap punya subjek, kata kerja dan tense sendiri. Tiga kata kerja **hanya** bisa di sini: *It is hoped / It was agreed / It has been decided that…* ('The rules are hoped to…' ✗).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rekan kerjamu meneruskan kabar tentang Dr. Wulan, peneliti di sebuah universitas di Yogyakarta.

options: Dr. Wulan is said that she is moving to Geneva.
It is said Dr. Wulan to be moving to Geneva.
It is said that Dr. Wulan is moving to Geneva.
question.explanation: Pola 1: **It is said that + kalimat lengkap** (*Dr. Wulan is moving…*). Pilihan pertama mencampur pola: kalau pakai *that*, mulai dengan **It**, bukan orangnya. Pilihan kedua menaruh to-infinitive setelah *It is said*, padahal pola 1 perlu *that* + kalimat lengkap.

steps.title: Pola 2: tiga bentuk infinitif
steps.text: Pola 2 diawali orang atau benda yang diberitakan. Infinitif sesudahnya menunjukkan kapan tindakannya terjadi.
steps.body:
**Subjek + be + kata kerja pelaporan + to-infinitive:**
- **to + bentuk dasar** = sekarang atau secara umum (dengan *expected*: nanti)
- **to be + -ing** = sedang berlangsung (*sedang*)
- **to have + bentuk ketiga** = lebih dulu (*sudah, kemarin*)
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia memakai satu kata kerja dan menambah kata waktu (*dikabarkan mengundurkan diri kemarin*). Bahasa Inggris menunjukkan waktunya di infinitif: 'is reported **resign** yesterday' ✗, 'is reported to resign yesterday' ✗ → *is reported **to have resigned** yesterday*.

steps.title: Kapan tindakannya terjadi?
steps.text: Ini infinitif-infinitifnya di satu garis. Masing-masing menunjukkan waktu tindakan dibandingkan dengan saat orang mengatakan atau meyakininya.

timeline.title: Infinitif menunjukkan waktunya
timeline.caption: Hitung dari saat klaimnya dibuat: is reported (sekarang) atau was reported (waktu itu).

steps.title: Berita yang sama, dua pola
steps.text: Perhatikan bagaimana kata kerja setelah that berubah jadi infinitif ketika orang atau bendanya pindah ke depan.
steps.body: Present → **to + bentuk dasar**; continuous → **to be + -ing**; past simple atau present perfect → **to have + bentuk ketiga**. Dengan kata kerja keadaan (*be, own, know, cost*), pakai to + bentuk dasar: *She is thought to own three hotels*, bukan 'to be owning'.

examples.id: Konon dia tinggal di Bali.

examples.en: It is believed that the bank is preparing a new app. → The bank is believed to be preparing a new app.
examples.id: Bank itu diyakini sedang menyiapkan aplikasi baru.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sebuah artikel tentang perusahaan terbuka di Jakarta. Tulis ulang beritanya dengan pola 2.

question.prompt: Ubah polanya: It is said that the director sold his shares before the announcement. → The director ___ his shares before the announcement.
question.explanation: Penjualannya terjadi **lebih dulu** (past simple *sold*, sebelum pengumuman) → **to have + bentuk ketiga**: *is said to have sold*. 'to sell' untuk sekarang atau secara umum, dan 'to sold' melanggar aturan: setelah *to*, bentuk dasar (*have*).

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sebuah judul berita bisnis. Katakan dalam bahasa Inggris, dengan pola 2.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Perusahaan itu diyakini sedang merencanakan PHK.
question.solution: The company is believed to be planning layoffs.
question.explanation: The company di depan, lalu **is believed** (diyakini). *sedang merencanakan* itu sedang berlangsung → **to be + -ing**: *to be planning*. PHK = **layoffs**.

steps.title: Pola 3: There is believed to be…
steps.text: Kalau beritanya adalah bahwa sesuatu ada, subjeknya there.
steps.body:
**There + is/are + kata kerja pelaporan + to be + kata benda.** Kata kerjanya mengikuti kata benda sesudahnya: *There **is** thought to be **a leak*** / *There **are** thought to be **two leaks***. Untuk yang lebih dulu: **to have been** (*There is said to have been an argument*).
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** di *Diduga **ada** masalah*, *ada* artinya *there is*, bukan *have*. 'There is believed **to have** a problem' ✗ → *There is believed **to be** a problem.*

pairs.en: There is said to have been…

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Seorang pemandu di taman nasional di Kalimantan bercerita kepada pengunjung tentang tanamannya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ more than 300 species of orchid in the park.
question.explanation: *ada* = there are, jadi infinitifnya **to be**, dan *300 species* itu jamak → **are**: *There are known to be*. 'There is' tidak cocok dengan kata benda jamak, dan 'to have' adalah jebakan kata *ada*.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini tiga polanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk laporan atau artikel beritamu berikutnya.

artifact.intro: Laporkan sebuah klaim tanpa menyebut siapa yang membuatnya atau menyatakan bahwa itu benar. be menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat; infinitifnya menunjukkan kapan tindakannya terjadi.
rows: It + be + bentuk ketiga + that + kalimat lengkap

It was reported that the flight had been delayed.

There + is/are + bentuk ketiga + to be
There is thought to be a leak in the pipe.

tips: Jangan campur polanya: **It … that** atau **subjek … to**. 'He is said that he left' ✗ → *It is said that he left* / *He is said to have left*.
Setelah **to**, bentuk dasar, dan waktunya masuk ke infinitif: 'is reported resign yesterday' ✗ → **is reported to have resigned** yesterday.
Setelah **there**, selalu **to be** (atau to have been), tidak pernah 'to have' + kata benda: *Diduga ada masalah* = *There is believed to be a problem*.
